newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends at seven-week high, awaits stoc.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends at seven-week high, awaits stoc.

text.p: Expectations of a further drawdown in LME stocks Friday propelled COMEX copper futures and their London counterparts up through key technical areas to close at a seven-week high, traders and analysts said.
"I think we are on a bit of a technical run, and we have projections of another large stock decline tomorrow," said William O'Neill of Merrill Lynch.
LME stocks have fallen by more than 100,000 tonnes in recent weeks, and brokers estimated stocks will tumble another 8,000 to 15,000 tonnes Friday.
LME stocks total 159,350 tonnes, well below a month's global supply.

COMEX stocks on Thursday rose 659 short tonnes to 23,856 short tons. Earlier in the week traders said some of the LME metal leaving Long Beach was going into COMEX's Arizona warehouses, the rest to U.S. consumers or to the Far East.
"In the short-term the performance of the market is very good," O'Neill said.
December COMEX settled 2.00 cents firmer at 94.95 cents per pound, traded 95.00 to 92.55 cents.
LME three months closed above the key psychological level of $2,000 per tonne.

Volume on COMEX was relatively good at an estimated 13,500 lots, compared to Wednesday's official 10,621 lots. Switches were estimated at 1,220 indicating that a good slice of activity was devoted to routine rollover of contracts as October nears expiry.
Gains in LME aluminum prices also injected some buoyancy into copper.

Meanwhile Phelps Dodge Corp's spokeswoman, Sue Suver said talks with labor unions representing employees at the company's Chino mine were due to resume mid to late morning, local time, in Las Cruces, New Mexico.
Suver said the union had asked for some clarification about what the company continued to describe as its final offer for a new three-year labor deal.
Union officials were unavailable for comment.
